34. In the light of above admitted facts of the present case, now I proceed to examine whether the policy in question in respect of the subject vehicle was obtained by the plaintiff from the defendant insurance company by way of misrepresentation and cheating.

35. At the cost of repetition, it may be noted here that insurance policy of the subject vehicle was in the name of wife of the plaintiff and during the period the insurance policy, Smt. Munesh Sharma,
wife of the plaintiff died on 05.05.2022, and after the expiry of the insurance policy and death of the wife of the plaintiff, the insurance policy was renewed for the period from 16.07.2022 till 15.07.2023 vide policy bearing No.3101991274 in the name of Smt. Munesh Sharma, wife of the plaintiff.
36.

The question before the Court for consideration is that there existed a valid contract of insurance between the plaintiff and the defendant when the insurance policy was renewed for the period from 16.07.2022 till 15.07.2023.
37.

sentences.text: What agreements are contracts.-

All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.

Nothing herein contained shall effect any law in force in [India] and not hereby expressly replealed,
by which any contract is required to be made in writing or in the presence of wintesses, or any law relating to the registration of documents.
38. In the light of provisions of section 10 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, the parties to the agreement must be competent to contract.
A valid contract may be made by natural persons, and by any other persons, who have a legal personality.

Whereas, in the present case, the insured Smt.
Munesh Sharma, wife of the plaintiff was not alive when the insurance policy was renewed for the period from 16.07.2022 to 15.07.2023 as she had already already died on 05.05.2022, therefore, one of the parties of the contract of insurance i.e. the insured was not competent for entering into a legally enforceable agreement.

Once it has been established that one of the parties to the agreement was not in the capacity of entering into an agreement, therefore, I am of the clear opinion that the agreement of insurance entered into by the plaintiff in the name of his deceased wife, which was effected from 16 July 2022 was not a legally enforceable agreement and the plaintiff cannot seek its enforcement in the Court of law against the defendant company.
39. Furthermore, the principle of uberrima fides applies in the present case rendering the contract null and void.

Uberrimae fidei or "uberrima RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR Date:

sentences.text: It requires parties to certain contracts to exercise the highest standard of full disclosure of any relevant conditions, circumstances, or risks to their counterparties.

Failing to disclose material facts that might influence the other party's decision when entering into a contract where uberrimae fidei applies can result in the contract being rendered null and void and the other party being released from any obligations under the contract.
40. Insurance contracts are the most common type of uberrimae fidei contracts.

Since the insurance company agrees to share the risk of loss with the policyholder, it is imperative that the policyholder act in good faith by fully disclosing all information that affects the insurance company's level of risk.

41. As I have noted above, the plaintiff has failed to disclose the material fact regarding death of Ms.
Munesh Sharma, wife of the plaintiff while entering into an agreement of insurance of the subject vehicle
, therefore, the contract of insurance involved in the present suit is hit by the principle of Ravinder Sharma vs Tata Aig Genaeral Insurance Company ...

On the other hand, in the present case the plaintiff is claiming amount from the defendant company on account of theft of the insured vehicle.

45. Since Ms. Munesh Sharma was not alive and already dead on the date when the current policy of insurance in respect of the subject vehicle was obtained from the defendant, therefore, I am of the clear opinion that the insurance policy on the basis of which the plaintiff is claiming recovery from the defendant on account of theft of the vehicle has been obtained by playing fraud and misrepresentation. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, in the present case, the insured Smt.
Munesh Sharma, wife of the plaintiff was not alive when the insurance policy was renewed for the period from 16.07.2022 to 15.07.2023 as she had already already died on 05.05.2022, therefore, one of the parties of the contract of insurance i.e. the insured was not competent for entering into a legally enforceable agreement.
Once it has been established that one of the parties to the agreement was not in the capacity of entering into an agreement, therefore, I am of the clear opinion that the agreement of insurance entered into by the plaintiff in the name of his deceased wife, which was effected from 16 July 2022 was not a legally enforceable agreement and the plaintiff cannot seek its enforcement in the Court of law against the defendant company.
39. Furthermore, the principle of uberrima fides applies in the present case rendering the contract null and void.

It requires parties to certain contracts to exercise the highest standard of full disclosure of any relevant conditions, circumstances, or risks to their counterparties.
Failing to disclose material facts that might influence the other party's decision when entering into a contract where uberrimae fidei applies can result in the contract being rendered null and void and the other party being released from any obligations under the contract.
Since the insurance company agrees to share the risk of loss with the policyholder, it is imperative that the policyholder act in good faith by fully disclosing all information that affects the insurance company's level of risk.
